rejected_as_false_positive.title: diff.patch truncated mid-hunk
rejected_as_false_positive.reason: FALSE POSITIVE — diff ends cleanly at 3368 lines on a complete run.odin hunk (normal unified-diff termination).

rejected_as_false_positive.title: CI invokes tools/harness.sh but no tools/* in diff
rejected_as_false_positive.reason: FALSE POSITIVE — tools/harness.sh was added in 0df9135 (Odin early prototype), an ancestor of the 1.1 merge; predates this PR, out of scope.

reviewer_agreement.title: Catalog fail-fast contract (ODN-5) is incomplete: content_host + the 'standard' tier are required by the fixture but never validated at load; app/harness discard the lookup `ok` and silently fall back to index 0
reviewer_agreement.location: core/catalog.odin (catalogs_load PROTO cross-check ~L176-181); app/main.odin:51,249-251; harness/catalogs.odin seed_fixture
reviewer_agreement.detail: File header promises 'missing required content abort', but only residential+router_basic are checked. If content_host/standard were removed from data/, the fixture silently spawns a wrong-type node / draws at tier 0 instead of aborting. Data is correct today so not a live break, but the fail-fast contract has a real gap.
reviewer_agreement.recommended_fix: Add `node_type_index(cat,"content_host")` + `pipe_tier_index(cat,"standard")` to catalogs_load's PROTO cross-check, and surface (don't discard) the lookup `ok` in the app/harness seed paths.

reviewer_agreement.title: The app layer (the story's deliverable) is the least-verified part: app.bin builds but no test RUNS it; the snap_node logic, the edit fast-path timing, and the app's fixture positions are unverified, and load_catalogs/seed_fixture are duplicated app<->harness with no shared contract so divergence is structurally undetectable
reviewer_agreement.detail: The verified replay-equality path is the HARNESS (pure action-log). The app's fast-path/snap/fixture are exercised only by a human. The app is never run in CI (GPU build needs a display). The harness is the designed headless workaround and shares core+render, which mitigates this — but the app's own glue is coverage debt on the new playable surface.
reviewer_agreement.recommended_fix: Either (a) extract the shared fixture into one place both app+harness call, and/or (b) add a headless (rlsw) smoke that drives the app's Command_Bus/snap path through the same core the harness verifies, so app/harness divergence becomes detectable.

reviewer_agreement.title: W1 drift-rejection covers header/parse/tag/truncation classes only; valid-parse PAYLOAD (hash-level) drift is never generated, and the replayed hashes from drift_check are discarded
reviewer_agreement.evidence: make_drift_mutations emits: catalog_hash@17, logic_hz@25, bad_magic@0, bad_version@4, bad_tag@41, truncated — all header/parse/tag/truncation. No mutation flips a draw payload {a,b,tier} to a different-but-valid-parse value.
reviewer_agreement.detail: Lens-guard #5 IS satisfied (W1 is a CI step and rejects 11/11 mutations). This is a deeper coverage extension: the replay gate's hash-level equality is asserted by verify_replay in `run`, not by the W1 negative test. Not a gap in the stated requirement.
reviewer_agreement.recommended_fix: Optionally add a payload mutation (flip a Cmd_Draw_Pipe endpoint to another live node id) and assert the replayed hashes DIVERGE from the manifest — exercising the hash-comparison path, not just log_read rejection.

reviewer_agreement.title: span_between's round-half-up branch is never exercised (every test/demo span is a perfect square) and the rounded-span compare is slightly more permissive than the documented 'compare squares' convention
reviewer_agreement.evidence:
core/topology.odin:
    r := isqrt(d2)
    if d2 - r*r > r { r += 1 }   // round half up — untested branch
    return i32(r)
validate_draw compares `span > max_span` (rounded), while project-context.md says 'no sqrt in the comparison path (compare squares)'.
reviewer_agreement.detail: A true distance of e.g. 14.4 rounds to 14 and passes max_span=14, where a d²>max_span² compare would reject. No live impact in 1.2 (fixture spans are exactly 12, far from any boundary; golden is blessed on actual behavior) — but the rounding branch is genuinely untested and the convention/code mismatch is real.
reviewer_agreement.recommended_fix: Add a non-perfect-square span to test_distance_metric_pinned (e.g. {0,0}->{3,5} → round(√34)=6, exercising the bump), and decide explicitly whether edit validation should compare d² to max_span² to match the documented convention.

reviewer_agreement.title: drift_check's truncation mutation underflows on a 0-byte blessed log: make([dynamic]u8, len(src)-1) gets a negative length and crashes instead of clean-rejecting
reviewer_agreement.evidence: trunc := make([dynamic]u8, len(src)-1, context.temp_allocator)  // no `if len(src) > 0` guard, unlike the other 5 mutations
reviewer_agreement.detail: Latent only — blessed logs are 33/71 bytes, never 0, so this cannot trigger on the current repo. If an empty log file ever appeared, drift-check would panic instead of reporting a clean rejection. The other five mutations are length-guarded; this one isn't.
reviewer_agreement.recommended_fix: Wrap the truncation mutation in `if len(src) > 1 { ... }` for consistency with the other mutations.

reviewer_agreement.title: jint narrows json.Integer (i64) to i32 with an unchecked cast; an out-of-range catalog value can wrap into the legal range and pass validation
reviewer_agreement.evidence: case json.Integer: return i32(x)   // x is i64; i32(x) wraps on overflow with no check
reviewer_agreement.detail: Catalogs are reviewed, checked-in data (not untrusted input) and most fields are range-checked after the cast, and catalog_hash binds the exact bytes. Still, a typo like logic_hz=5000000000 would wrap to a value that could land in 1..1000 and pass. Defense-in-depth, not a live bug.
reviewer_agreement.recommended_fix: Range-check the i64 before narrowing (reject if outside i32 min/max, or per-field bounds), to honor the ODN-5 fail-fast contract fully.

findings.title: draw_text truncates each rune to u8 — the em dash in the window title renders as a garbage control byte
findings.evidence: for c in txt { append(&cbuf, u8(c)) }   // string iterates runes; u8('—')==0x14
findings.detail: The HUD title 'Packet Plumber — v2 story 1.2' mangles the em dash to 0x14. Cosmetic only — HUD text is app-layer, not in state or any T2 golden (goldens capture draw_world with drag={}, no HUD).
findings.recommended_fix: Copy the string bytes directly (append the []u8 of the string) instead of iterating runes, or restrict HUD strings to ASCII.

findings.title: Fiber 'glowing inner core' is a no-op: it draws pipe_fiber over pipe_fiber; palette.json's pipe_core is never read
findings.evidence: if pipe_tiers[...].id == "wide" { rl.DrawLineEx(a, b, width*0.45, v.palette.pipe_fiber) }  // tier_pipe_color("wide") ALSO returns pipe_fiber
findings.detail: The inner core uses the same color as the outer pipe, so the 'glow' is invisible, and the lighter pipe_core color sits unused in palette.json. Latent in 1.2 (the fixture draws 'standard', never 'wide'; the golden doesn't hit this path), but the code is wrong for when wide pipes are drawn.
findings.recommended_fix: Draw the inner core with v.palette.pipe_core (the lighter blue) instead of pipe_fiber.

findings.title: draw_ghost shows green (ghost_ok / 'would validate') even when there is no snap target — slightly misleading drag preview
findings.evidence: drag.valid defaults to .None on no-target; draw_ghost: col = ghost_ok; if drag.valid != .None { col = ghost_bad }  → no-target = green
findings.detail: Dragging into empty space shows a green ghost implying 'valid', but releasing there commits nothing (drag_to==0). Functionally harmless (no bad pipe created); purely a preview-color nuance.
findings.recommended_fix: Use a neutral/ghost dim color when drag_to==0, reserve green for a real snapped+validatable target.

findings.title: Draw_Intent.tier comment promises a 'default standard' the parser never applies
findings.evidence: tier: string, // pipe_tiers id (narrow/standard/wide); default "standard"   — but parse_demo sets tier=fields[5] with no default
findings.detail: parse_demo requires `at <n>ms draw <from> <to> <tier>` (>=6 fields), so a tierless draw is a parse error, not defaulted. The comment is misleading; there is no default path.
findings.recommended_fix: Either implement the default (if fields[5] missing/empty → "standard") or drop the comment.

findings.title: App.res_id / rt_id / host_id are write-only — seeded but never read
findings.evidence: app.res_id, app.rt_id, app.host_id = seed_fixture(&app.state, &cat)   // assigned; no read site (handle_input uses drag.from_node / drag_to)
findings.detail: The three node-id fields are stored and never consumed. Dead state; harmless but invites confusion about the intended draw source.
findings.recommended_fix: Remove the three fields (and the tuple assignment) unless a later story consumes them.

findings.title: app/main.odin never calls run_destroy on its Run_State (only catalogs_destroy + CloseWindow are deferred)
findings.evidence: defer pp.catalogs_destroy(&cat) / defer rl.CloseWindow()  — but app.state (Run_State with action_log, events, topology arrays) is never freed
findings.detail: Moot for a game process (the OS reclaims everything on exit), but inconsistent with the explicit defer pattern used for catalogs/window. No leak in practice.
findings.recommended_fix: Add `defer pp.run_destroy(&app.state)` for symmetry, or note that process-exit reclamation is intentional for the app.

findings.title: T2 capture times that quantize to tick 0 or past the last tick are silently never captured — no golden compared/written, demo still passes
findings.evidence: cap_tick := u64(max(0, i64(cap_ms)*i64(hz)/1000)); if cap_tick == tick { ... }   // tick starts at 1; cap_tick==0 never matches; cap_tick>ticks never matches
findings.detail: A mis-authored capture time (0ms, or beyond run_ms) is silently skipped with no fail. The shipped draw.dem is fine (capture at 2500ms → tick 50 ≤ 60). Latent authoring-safety gap.
findings.recommended_fix: Validate demo captures against [1, ticks] at parse time and fail loud if any falls outside.

findings.title: Draw intents with at_ms beyond run_ms become dead log records — applied never, but silently accepted into the blessed log + replay
findings.evidence: apply_tick = floor(at_ms*hz/1000)+1  — if > ticks, the command is logged but never matched in the step loop
findings.detail: A demo draw after run_ms is inert but still serialized into draw.log.bin and replayed (also inertly). Not a divergence (live and replay agree on 'never applied'), but a quiet authoring trap. Shipped draw.dem is fine.
findings.recommended_fix: Validate intent times <= run_ms at parse time.

findings.title: dist2 widens to i64 AFTER the i32 subtraction — node coordinates spanning >= 2^31 wrap before the square
findings.evidence: dx := i64(a[0] - b[0])   // a[0]-b[0] is i32, overflows before the i64 widen
findings.detail: Theoretical only — positions are grid tiles on a 40x30 map; they never approach 2^31. The idiomatic fix is `i64(a[0]) - i64(b[0])`. Pinned metric stays exact for any realistic map.
findings.recommended_fix: Widen before subtracting: `dx := i64(a[0]) - i64(b[0])`.

findings.title: Self-loop drag is filtered before validation in the app — .Self_Loop never surfaces in the UI (silent no-op instead of a rejection hint)
findings.evidence: if id, ok := snap_node(...); ok && id != app.drag.from_node { ... }   // dragging back onto the source never sets drag_to, so validate_draw is never called with a==b
findings.detail: The core rejects a==b (test_draw_rejects_self_loop passes), but the app pre-empts it: a node→itself drag releases with drag_to==0, so nothing happens and no 'self-loop' hint shows. Functionally correct (no self-pipe), just no user feedback.
findings.recommended_fix: If a visible self-loop rejection is desired, detect `id == from_node` and show reject_label(.Self_Loop) on the ghost.

findings.title: node_slot_raw returns slot 0 for an unmatched id (latent wrong-state trap if a caller ever skips validate_draw)
findings.evidence:
for i in 0..<len(t.node_alive) { if t.node_id[i] == id { return u32(i) } }
    return 0 // unreachable when called post-validate
findings.detail: apply_draw calls node_slot_raw only after validate_draw confirmed both endpoints exist, so the fallback is unreachable on the current path. If a future caller skipped validation, it would silently target node 0 (not OOB — slot 0 exists). Defensive observation, not a live bug.
findings.recommended_fix: Make node_slot_raw return (u32, bool) and have apply_draw assert/abort on miss, so the 'unreachable' can't silently corrupt state.

findings.title: Demo names flow unsanitized into golden/tmp write paths — path traversal is CLI-reachable (harness run|save|replay <name>), though not from the CI demos/ listing
findings.evidence: log_path: fmt.tprintf("goldens/%s.log.bin", demo)   / golden_path: fmt.tprintf("goldens/%s/%05dms.png", demo, ms)   / drift tmp: fmt.tprintf("/tmp/pp-drift-%s-%s.bin", name, m.label)
findings.detail: A CLI caller passing `../../x` as the demo name writes outside goldens/. Not reachable from CI (which lists demos/ filenames) and this is a local dev tool, so impact is low — defense-in-depth only.
findings.recommended_fix: Reject demo names containing '/' or '..' at the CLI boundary.

findings.title: step applies commands one-by-one, not as an arch §6.1/E23 atomic batch (forward-looking — no multi-command batch exists in 1.2)
findings.evidence: for cmd in commands { _, err := topology_apply_edit(&state.topology, cmd, cat); ... }   // per-command, not validate-all-then-apply
findings.detail: Arch §6.1 specifies topology_apply_edit as validate-all-then-apply for batches (E23, e.g. atomic junction-demolish). In 1.2 every tick carries 0-1 single draws, so there is no batch to be non-atomic about. Becomes relevant when demolish/multi-command batches land.
findings.recommended_fix: When the first multi-command batch (demolish) lands, route the tick's commands through a validate-all-then-apply path so partial application can't happen.

findings.title: 'A rejected draw mutates nothing' is asserted for 3 of 5 rejection tests — the unknown-tier and missing-node cases omit the pipe_count==0 check
findings.evidence: test_draw_rejects_unknown_tier_and_missing_node checks err == .Unknown_Tier / .Missing_Node but does not assert pipe_count==0 after each
findings.detail: Minor: the no-mutation guarantee is pinned for self-loop/terminal/span but not for the unknown-tier/missing-node rejections. apply_draw is only reachable post-validate, so they can't mutate — but the test doesn't prove it.
findings.recommended_fix: Add `pipe_count == 0` assertions after the two rejections for parity with the other three.

findings.title: E11 never-recycled-on-demolish half is untestable in 1.2 (no demolish command) — the tombstone/alive=false serialization path is dead code until demolish
findings.evidence: serialize writes w_bool(t.node_alive[i]) / w_bool(t.pipe_alive[i]) for every slot — but nothing in 1.2 ever sets alive=false (no demolish), so every slot is true
findings.detail: The monotonic-id half of E11 is tested; the tombstone-serialization half (alive=false riding in the hash) is unexercised because demolish is story 1.x. Forward-looking coverage gap, not a 1.2 defect.
findings.recommended_fix: When demolish lands, add the tombstone test (demolish a node/pipe, assert its id is never reused and its alive=false rides in the hash).

findings.title: From-scratch (lens-guard #7) VERIFIED CLEAN: 1.2 view.odin (260 lines) and topology.odin are fresh, distinct implementations vs the reference Odin tree's view.odin (441 lines) — no wholesale copy
findings.location: app/render/view.odin vs /Users/moses/code/packet-plumber-prototype-ref/app/render/view.odin; core/topology.odin vs ref core/topology.odin
findings.evidence: ref view.odin header: 'Reads ONLY the immutable snapshot (ODN-1)... pulse shapes are a pinned triangle wave' (441 lines, has hud/map/audio). 1.2 view.odin header: 'Reads ONLY the topology... STATIC map' (260 lines, 1.2-scoped). Distinct scope, distinct headers, different line counts.
findings.detail: The 'prototype-ref' is the project's own evolved Odin tree (not Godot). 1.2 is a smaller, freshly-written 1.2-scoped implementation. Data-value reuse (pipe-tier numbers) is allowed. Lens-guard #7 holds — this entry records the positive verification, not a defect.
findings.recommended_fix: No action — recorded for traceability.

findings.title: Advisory test gate: CONCERNS (tests lens rated FAIL on coverage, downgraded — the load-bearing P0 replay-equality IS verified; the gaps are app-layer coverage)
findings.evidence: tests lens advisory: P0 app fast-path/snap untested → gate FAIL. Re-triaged: the E10 replay-equality mechanism IS verified (test_replay_byte_identical + harness draw demo); app-binary execution is constrained by GPU/CI (the rlsw harness is the designed headless proxy).
findings.detail: Recorded as the tests lens's coverage opinion. Does not escalate to a blocker: no load-bearing lens-guard is violated and all gates are green. The underlying app-layer coverage concern is captured in the 'app layer under-verified' warning.
findings.recommended_fix: See the app-coverage-gap warning.

verdict_reason: 0 blockers. Every load-bearing lens-guard holds: replay-equality-over-draw verified (test_replay_byte_identical draws 2 pipes + harness draw demo, byte-identical replay); ODN-1 core engine-free (grep + lint gate 1 clean); ODN-10 integer/no-map-iteration (lint gate 3 clean); T2 pixel golden byte-exact (compare_images pa[i]!=pb[i], golden present, harness run green); W1 CI negative test actually in CI and rejects 11/11 drifts; from-scratch verified clean. All 5 gates green at the reviewed sha. The 2 warnings (catalog fail-fast incomplete; app layer under-verified) are real but addressable in 1.3 and do not violate any spine invariant.
